messages:
jordan: Quick heads-up — the cost dashboard is showing weird negative cache savings for a handful of tenants after the last canary :confused:
kai: ugh, saw that too. looks like prefetch credits got double-applied in the amortization step :grimacing:
maria: do we have a repro? which tenants, sample rate, timeframe?
jordan: @maria i pulled a sample: tenant_id t-893, window 2026-03-17..2026-03-18. spike in "prefetch_credit_applied" + negative 'net_token_cost' on per-route panel
alex: could be the backfill job that ran last night — it emits credits as "prefetch:backfill" and the vizing SQL groups on credit_type only, so backfill + regular prefetch both count
kai: yeah, the backend charge calculation treats credits as a set of tags and then sums naive. we should be tokenizing credit_lineage before rollup
paul: suggested quick fix: when aggregating, dedupe by (origin_id, request_signature) for credits issued within 24h. that would prevent duplicates from backfill
nori: would that break legitimate multi-credit flows (e.g., a true prefetch + a later cache-eviction rebate)? :thinking:
paul: maybe, need a policy: prefer explicit "reason" precedence — backfill < prefetch < rebate. and expose that precedence in the schema so UI can explain it
maria: for the dashboard change we need two things: 1) fix dedupe in charge calc; 2) add an explain row in the UI for any negative-sum tenants showing contributing credits and their provenance :eyes:
ops-bot: deploy pipeline: job "billing-rollup" failed on canary-3 2h ago — see https://ci.internal/reports/6821
alex: ops-bot thx — that job did the backfill. i'll open a patch to the rollup to add origin_id dedupe and add a debug flag to dump raw credit events
jordan: ideal UX: per-tenant sparklines with a hover show: token-burn, cache-savings, backfill-credits, model-sku cost. plus a tiny "counterfactual" toggle that shows cost if prefetch credits were not applied
kai: counterfactual toggle is great for product to see rollout impact. backend API sketch: 
```
GET /internal/v1/cost-preview?tenant=t-893&window=24h&counterfactual=prefetch
Response: { "token_cost": 12345, "cache_savings": -4000, "prefetch_credits": 4500, "counterfactual_net": 12345 - 4500 }
```
alex: don't love arithmetic in string response :) prefer explicit numbers, e.g. "counterfactual_net": 7845. also need provenance array for UI so we can show "why negative"
maria: agreed. provenance array with limited cardinality (top 10) and an aggregate "others" bucket to keep the UI snappy
paul: note on sampling: some tenants are sampled at 10% for the econ panels. we need to extrapolate credits carefully or the counterfactual will be noisy
nori: can we add a per-model tail-cost column? certain LlamaX variants have crazy tail token overhead due to attention overhead and we're hiding that in per-route averages
jordan: yes — add per-model average token cost, and per-invocation 95p latency tax (so teams can see "this model incurs extra token cost due to long tails")
kai: rollout UX thought: when a new model is rolled out as canary, the preview slider should show projected unit-cost delta at current traffic + projected 5% and 20% traffic splits. product folks asked for that yesterday
maria: product also wants a colour-coded certainty badge (green/orange/red) based on sample size and cache credit staleness. red if <200 invocations or >12h since last rollup
ori: operational concern: adding these extra provenance arrays will increase payload sizes. we should make that opt-in via ?detail=provenance (default minimal)
paul: +1. and add a sampling_version header so we can iterate without breaking clients
alex: i put a tiny PoC in a branch: /internal/cost-preview v0.2, includes provenance + counterfactual toggles and detail param. i'll add tests and a feature-flag
jordan: canary plan: roll to canary-2 with debug enabled for 2 hours, collect screenshots of the UI diffs, then flip fix on canary-3 where the backfill ran
kai: quick checklist: 
- patch rollup to dedupe origin_id (paul)
- add sampling_version header + extrapolation doc (maria)
- backend cost-preview API v0.2 (alex)
- UI explain row + counterfactual toggle + certainty badge (jordan, product)
- run canary with debug, validate t-893, t-441, and t-1023

maria: timeline? this is visible in dashboards and chasing product tickets. ideally a hotfix today, full rollout tomorrow
paul: i'll open the rollup PR now and mark it urgent
jordan: thanks all. assign owners as above. post screenshots here once canary runs so we can confirm negative numbers go away :thumbsup:
alex: opened PR #8245 — link https://git.internal/p/r/redwood/billing/8245 
ops-bot: PR #8245 merged into canary-2 by alex (ci: green)
kai: running the debug canary now, will report back in ~30m
maria: if anyone from support needs an explanation to customers, draft a short blurb: "We observed duplicate prefetch credits caused by a backfill job; impact was on displayed cache-saving numbers only. We deployed a fix to deduplicate credits; billing charged to customers is unaffected."
jordan: perfect blurb. saving to /snippets/support/cache_credit_backfill.md
paul: can confirm t-893 now shows cache_savings 0 -> 420 after the fix, and no negative net cost in the 24h panel
ori: nice. closing the ticket once canary is green and UI cert badge goes green for sampled tenants
alex: 🍾
